questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: Only Allah truly deserves worship, and no one can share that with Him.

questions.question: What do different groups of people naturally do in the passage?
questions.answer: They turn to different kinds of worship.

questions.question: Besides people, what other kinds of things are said to worship in their own way?
questions.answer: Animals and even non-living things.

questions.question: How do blessings and gifts in the world affect people?
questions.answer: They lead people to thank, praise, and worship.

questions.question: What unseen things are named as signs pointing to worship of one Allah?
questions.answer: Spiritual signs, revelation, and inspiration.

questions.question: According to the passage, how many gods are fit to be worshipped?
questions.answer: Only one.

questions.question: What does the passage say these signs prove about Divinity?
questions.answer: They show one complete and ruling Divinity.

questions.question: Why can this Divinity not have a partner?
questions.answer: Because true worship belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: In the passage, what special place do conscious living beings have in the world?
questions.answer: They are described as the highest fruits of creation.

questions.question: What bad thing would happen if others made people forget Allah?
questions.answer: People would turn away from the One they should worship.

questions.question: Why might people forget their true Lord quickly, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because they do not see Him with their eyes.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an speak against worshipping others with Allah?
questions.answer: It strongly rejects it and warns about Hell.

questions.question: What truth is being explained in this passage?
questions.answer: The truth of absolute Divinity.

questions.question: What do people’s natural ways of worship show?
questions.answer: They show that worship is a real part of how people were made.

questions.question: How do animals and non-living things worship, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They do it by carrying out the jobs given to them.

questions.question: What do the many blessings in the universe invite people to do?
questions.answer: To be thankful and to worship Allah.

questions.question: What do revelation and inspiration agree about?
questions.answer: That only Allah deserves worship.

questions.question: What does the passage say all these signs prove together?
questions.answer: They prove one true Divinity over all.

questions.question: If true Divinity is real, what can it never accept?
questions.answer: It can never accept partners.

questions.question: Why are conscious living beings important in this argument?
questions.answer: Because they are the ones who can knowingly thank and worship.

questions.question: What would be wrong if another being made people feel thankful to it instead of Allah?
questions.answer: It would pull them away from their real Lord.

questions.question: Why would that be against the purpose of Divinity?
questions.answer: Because Divinity calls people to worship Allah alone.

questions.question: What does the passage help us understand about shirk?
questions.answer: It is very wrong because it gives worship to others besides Allah.

questions.question: Why does the Qur’an strongly warn people who do shirk?
questions.answer: Because sharing worship with others goes against the truth of Divinity.

questions.question: Who alone is worthy of worship in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah alone.

questions.question: What do many kinds of worship in the world point to?
questions.answer: They point to one true Lord.

questions.question: What is one way non-human creatures show worship?
questions.answer: They follow the work they were created to do.

questions.question: When people receive gifts and blessings, what should that bring out in them?
questions.answer: Thankfulness, praise, and worship.

questions.question: What kind of signs besides visible things are mentioned?
questions.answer: Hidden spiritual signs like revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What can we infer from all these signs working together?
questions.answer: They all agree on the same truth about Allah alone being worshipped.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect worship with conscious living beings?
questions.answer: Because they can understand blessings and answer with thanks.

questions.question: What would happen if people were turned away from Allah to others?
questions.answer: They would forget the One they are meant to worship.

questions.question: Why is forgetting Allah described as something that could happen quickly?
questions.answer: Because Allah is not seen by people in this life.

questions.question: Would letting others share worship fit the holiness of Divinity?
questions.answer: No, it would go against it.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect idea is shown about blessings?
questions.answer: Blessings should lead people to gratitude and worship.

questions.question: What is the result in the Qur’an for insisting on false worship?
questions.answer: A strong warning of Hell.

questions.question: What title is given to the truth in this passage?
questions.answer: Absolute Divinity.

questions.question: What does “absolute” help us understand here?
questions.answer: That Allah’s right to be worshipped is complete and shared with no one.

questions.question: What do human beings do because of how they were created?
questions.answer: They worship in ways that fit their nature.

questions.question: How do the rest of creation also show a kind of worship?
questions.answer: They serve through the tasks and roles given to them.

questions.question: What feelings should gifts in the world grow in people’s hearts?
questions.answer: Thanks and praise.

questions.question: What three unseen helps are named as witnesses to this truth?
questions.answer: Spiritual signs, revelation, and inspiration.

questions.question: What do all these witnesses say together?
questions.answer: That worship belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: In the picture used by the passage, what are conscious living beings compared to?
questions.answer: The finest fruits at the top of a tree.

questions.question: Why is that comparison important?
questions.answer: It shows they have a special job to respond with worship and thanks.

questions.question: What would be the problem if others made those beings feel grateful to them instead?
questions.answer: It would steal worship from where it belongs.

questions.question: What does this teach about worshipping anyone besides Allah?
questions.answer: It is false and not allowed.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an respond to that false belief?
questions.answer: It rejects it strongly and gives a serious warning.

questions.question: What does the passage say is shown in a very clear way?
questions.answer: The rule and reality of one Divinity.

questions.question: Name one kind of evidence from human life in the passage.
questions.answer: People have natural ways of worship.

questions.question: Name one kind of evidence from other creatures in the passage.
questions.answer: Animals worship by doing their created functions.

questions.question: Name one kind of evidence from the gifts in the world.
questions.answer: Blessings move people to be thankful.

questions.question: Name one kind of evidence from the unseen.
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What single truth do all these different proofs support?
questions.answer: That Allah alone deserves worship.

questions.question: What does the passage say about having a partner with Allah in worship?
questions.answer: It can never be accepted.

questions.question: Why are humans especially important in this matter?
questions.answer: Because they can knowingly give thanks and worship.

questions.question: What wrong direction could people take if they were fooled by others?
questions.answer: They could turn from Allah to false objects of worship.

questions.question: Why is that especially dangerous?
questions.answer: Because people might forget their true Lord.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the purpose of blessings?
questions.answer: They are meant to guide people to Allah.

questions.question: Why does the Qur’an speak so often against polytheism?
questions.answer: Because it opposes the truth that only Allah should be worshipped.

questions.question: What is the first truth teaching us about Allah?
questions.answer: Allah has the full right to be worshipped.

questions.question: What do people’s natural acts of worship tell us?
questions.answer: Worship is built into human life.

questions.question: How do creatures without words still show worship?
questions.answer: They do what they were made to do.

questions.question: What should a person do after seeing many gifts from Allah?
questions.answer: Thank Him, praise Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What do revelation and inspiration help people understand?
questions.answer: That only Allah is worthy of worship.

questions.question: What big conclusion does the passage make from all these signs?
questions.answer: There is one absolute Divinity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about sharing that Divinity?
questions.answer: It cannot be shared.

questions.question: Why are living, aware beings called the fruits of creation?
questions.answer: Because they are meant to answer blessings with worship.

questions.question: What would others be doing wrong if they made people feel deeply thankful to them instead of Allah?
questions.answer: They would be taking hearts away from the true object of worship.

questions.question: Why would that clash with the meaning of Divinity?
questions.answer: Because Divinity’s holy purpose is worship of Allah alone.

questions.question: What lesson should a Muslim child take from this passage?
questions.answer: We should worship only Allah and thank Him for His gifts.

questions.question: What final warning from the passage explains the seriousness of this matter?
questions.answer: The Qur’an strongly warns those who give worship to others besides Allah.
